title_en: October 2026 JOGMEC amendment bill: oil transport investment and carbon capture support

quick_take.what_changed: The Cabinet's bill would add oil-transport investment and grants for carbon dioxide capture, transport and storage to JOGMEC's statutory activities.
quick_take.who_is_affected: Energy resource developers, oil transport projects, and carbon capture and storage sponsors could be affected if the bill becomes law.
quick_take.what_to_do_now: Monitor the bill and any changes in the Diet; do not treat proposed JOGMEC support as an available programme yet.

watch_pages.label: House of Representatives: JOGMEC amendment bill

paragraphs: The Cabinet Legislation Bureau explains that international conditions have increased the importance of secure energy and metal mineral supplies. The government proposes to strengthen the support available for Japanese companies to secure those resources.

The bill would expand JOGMEC's functions to include investment relating to oil transportation and grants for funding carbon dioxide capture, transport and storage. These are proposed public support functions; they do not themselves impose new obligations on private project sponsors.

The proposal also sits alongside Japan's existing carbon storage policy, but it is a separate legislative initiative. METI reported in June 2024 that JOGMEC had selected nine advanced CCS projects aimed at developing replicable business models and starting operations by 2030. That earlier project selection illustrates the policy context; it does not establish eligibility for the new grants contemplated by the October 2026 bill.

The Cabinet approved and submitted the proposal on 13 October 2026 as Cabinet Bill No. 13 in the 222nd Diet. The House of Representatives' official record does not show enactment or promulgation as of this verification.

expected: The Diet may examine and amend the bill before voting. If both Houses pass it, an enacted Act is promulgated and enters into force according to its supplementary provisions or an implementing order. This is not a forecast of passage.
uncertainties: The bill has no enacted amendment Act number or confirmed commencement date.
Funding eligibility, grant conditions and implementation budgets are not established by the materials reviewed.

paragraphs: Energy transport and carbon capture project sponsors may assess whether the proposed functions would create a future funding opportunity. A submitted bill alone provides no right to apply for those proposed new functions.
checklist: Check the official Diet status and amendments to the bill.
Map any planned oil transportation or carbon capture, transport and storage investment to the proposed functions.
Wait for enacted legislation and implementing rules before assuming that new JOGMEC support is available.
